name: Aster
lede: Aster is a muted violet named for the star-shaped flower, recorded in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary of color and dated there to 1916.

sections.title: The flower
sections.body:
Aster is the name of a family of daisy-like garden flowers. Baty's color catalogue pairs the shade Purple Aster with amethyst as its mineral match in the violet-purple series [1]. Its list of purples also names the pansy and the sweet-scented violet among flower colors [1]. A short-day plant, the aster blooms as autumn days shorten, a fact Birren cites from a 1938 article [2].

The color itself is a greyed violet, nearest to [[plum]] among everyday names, 12.1 units away [3]. Related colors are [[amethyst]], [[lilac]] and [[violet]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The library has one source for Aster, Maerz & Paul 1930, which dates it to 1916 and files it under fashion and textiles [3]. In the archive, 14 of 23,781 paintings carry it [4]. That is too few to say anything, so we do not claim a trend, and no painter or school stands out in so small a sample [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished works [4].
